messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want:

1. In New York (NY), libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles (LA), libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago, libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects a single argument object with location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe". But the facilities field seems to accept only one value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is union of those strings. That suggests we can only pass one facility at a time. But we need multiple facilities per query. The function signature might not support multiple facilities. However, maybe we can pass an array? The type says "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". Wait, the type shows "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[],", but the syntax is ambiguous. It might mean facilities can be either one of those strings or an array of them. The type annotation is weird: "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[],", but the trailing comma indicates it's part of the object. The type might be a union of string or array of strings. So we can pass an array of strings.

Thus we should call the function three times, each with location and facilities array.

We need to produce calls to the function. According to guidelines, we should output JSON with name and arguments. We need to do it for each location. The assistant can call the function multiple times. We should produce separate calls. The assistant should not provide additional text besides the function calls. So we will produce three function calls.

We need to format as JSON. The function name is public_library_find_nearby. The arguments: location: string, facilities: array of strings.

So first call: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Second: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Third: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to output each call separately. The guidelines say we should output a single JSON object with name and arguments. But we have multiple calls. We can output multiple calls sequentially. The system may interpret each call separately. We'll output each call as separate JSON objects. The assistant should not add explanatory text. Just the calls.

Thus we produce:

{
"name": "public_library_find_nearby",
"arguments": {
"location": "New York, NY",
"facilities": ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
}
}

Then next call.
